items.title: fix: preserve approval sandbox decisions in unified exec
fix: sandbox zsh fork unified exec trampoline

observed_change: Codex preserves approved sandbox-escalation decisions through unified-exec launch and intercepted shell exec paths while keeping bounded additional-permission requests sandboxed.
changed_surfaces: unified exec runtime launch sandbox selection
managed-network environment handling for unsandboxed execs
user_visible_path: A Codex user running unified exec with zsh-fork, `sandbox_permissions=require_escalated`, or exec-policy sandbox bypass can now have the approved sandbox decision applied to the shell launch path and intercepted execs; bounded `with_additional_permissions` requests remain sandboxed rather than becoming full unsandboxed overrides.
control_plane_relevance: Decodex should preserve the exact upstream `sandbox_permissions` mode when invoking or explaining Codex execution, because `UseDefault`, `RequireEscalated`, and `WithAdditionalPermissions` now intentionally route through different escalation behavior.
compatibility_risk: Moderate for automation or UI layers that collapse sandbox permission modes, infer network proxy state from older unified-exec behavior, or treat additional permissions as equivalent to full escalation.
adoption_opportunity: Use this as a compatibility note for Decodex sandbox and approval readbacks: approved escalation should survive unified-exec setup, while additional permissions should still be reported as bounded sandbox expansion.
community_value: High for operators who depend on precise sandbox and approval semantics, because the change fixes a subtle mismatch between user-approved escalation and the actual unified-exec launch path.
deprecated_or_breaking_notes: No user-facing deprecation is introduced; the behavior changes the effective sandbox decision for previously approved unified-exec launches and intercepted execs.
evidence: PR #24981 states that zsh-fork unified exec could do meaningful work before an intercepted child `execv(2)` existed and therefore lost approved parent sandbox decisions.

codex-rs/core/src/tools/runtimes/unified_exec.rs derives `launch_sandbox_permissions` separately from the request and runtime filesystem policy, then uses it for managed-network, environment, and launch sandbox selection.

codex-rs/core/src/tools/runtimes/shell/unix_escalation.rs now switches explicitly on `SandboxPermissions::UseDefault`, `RequireEscalated`, and `WithAdditionalPermissions` when deciding whether intercepted execs need escalation.
The PR notes unsandboxed intercepted execs rebuild the environment as `RequireEscalated`, stripping managed-network proxy variables consistently with other unsandboxed execution.

codex-rs/core/tests/suite/unified_exec_zsh_fork_approvals.rs adds Unix coverage for preserved parent approval, policy bypass, bounded additional permissions, denied-read preservation, intercepted-exec prompts, and managed-network environment stripping.
The normalized bundle artifacts/github/bundles/openai-codex-pr-24981.json records 6 changed files for the merged PR.
caveats: The fix is scoped to unified-exec and intercepted shell execution semantics; it does not grant broader unsandboxed authority beyond approved or policy-allowed cases.

next_actions.reason: Sandbox-mode preservation is a Decodex Control Plane compatibility concern.
The fix has a clear operator-facing explanation for precise sandbox and approval behavior.
